name: Penetration Testing Middle East
core: Web and mobile application, internal infrastructure and external infrastructure penetration testing
acc: Dubai Cyber Force membership stated by the company; consultant certifications stated by the company
delivery: Project-based: scoping call, signed proposal, testing, debrief
other: Remediation assistance if agreed in advance
best: Pentest-only engagements covering web, mobile and infrastructure
body: Penetration Testing Middle East is a pentest-focused firm that provides web application, mobile application, internal infrastructure and external infrastructure penetration testing. The company states that it was established in mid-2023, is based in Dubai Silicon Oasis and serves the UAE. It describes itself as one of the first companies to join the Dubai Cyber Force initiative, a scheme run by DESC with CREST. Its About page lists consultant certifications such as OSCP, OSCE, OSWE, OSED, CREST CCT APP and CREST CRT. Engagements begin with a scoping call and a signed proposal, include safe proof-of-concept demonstrations of exploited vulnerabilities, and close with an executive and technical debrief. Remediation assistance is offered if agreed in advance.

name: ValueMentor
core: Application, network, mobile, API, segmentation, cloud, wireless and continuous testing; red teaming; OT, IoT and AI security testing
acc: DESC, CREST and PCI QSA labels shown on its site (stated by the company); Dubai Cyber Force approval named in a CREST announcement, January 2024
other: Compliance and privacy advisory, virtual CISO, SOC as a service, managed detection and response
best: Testing mapped to PCI, SWIFT or sector compliance programmes
body: ValueMentor is a cybersecurity services firm that provides penetration testing, red teaming and compliance-driven security testing. Its site lists application, network, mobile, API, segmentation, cloud, wireless and continuous testing, and red team scenarios covering assumed breach, social engineering, physical security and ransomware simulation. It also lists OT and IoT testing, AI model and LLM application testing, and test programmes for PCI, SWIFT and ADHICS. The site displays DESC, CREST and PCI QSA labels, and a CREST announcement of January 2024 names ValueMentor among the first Dubai Cyber Force approvals. Beyond testing, ValueMentor lists privacy services, virtual CISO, VARA compliance advisory and managed security, including SOC as a service.

name: Paranoid Security
core: Manual web and mobile application audits, external and internal penetration tests, Wi-Fi audits, red teaming, social engineering
delivery: Project-based manual testing led by a senior specialist (stated by the company)
other: Crypto wallet forensics and blockchain tracing, cyber exercises, security awareness training
best: Specialist-led manual testing for fintech, crypto and corporate teams
body: Paranoid Security is a boutique offensive security team that provides manual penetration testing, red team operations and crypto forensics. The company states that its testing scope covers web and mobile application audits, external and internal perimeter tests, Wi-Fi audits and social engineering. According to the company, a senior specialist leads each project and reports include proof-of-concept evidence, CVSS scores and a remediation plan. Its technical blog publishes monthly Microsoft patch analysis, and the company states that its specialists hold CVE credits at major international vendors, some under NDA. Paranoid Security serves fintech, crypto and corporate clients in the UAE. Its crypto forensics work covers wallet analysis and blockchain tracing.

name: DTS Solution
core: Penetration testing, red teaming and adversary emulation, web and mobile testing, wireless testing, social engineering, OSINT
acc: CREST penetration testing and incident response; Dubai Cyber Force partner-assured services (listed in CREST marketplace, checked November 2026)
delivery: Project-based testing alongside a 24x7 managed SOC
other: Managed SOC (HawkEye), GRC consulting, incident response and digital forensics
best: Testing and managed monitoring from one provider
body: DTS Solution is a cybersecurity firm that provides penetration testing, red teaming and adversary emulation alongside managed security. Its site lists vulnerability assessment, web and mobile application testing, wireless testing, social engineering and OSINT under offensive security, and a Dubai office on Sheikh Zayed Road. The CREST marketplace lists the company with penetration testing and incident response accreditation and Dubai Cyber Force partner-assured services, checked November 2026. The same listing calls DTS a Beyon Cyber company, and the company's site states that Beyon Cyber agreed to acquire a majority stake. Other services include a managed SOC called HawkEye, GRC consulting and digital forensics.

name: Wattlecorp Cybersecurity Labs
base: UAE listed among locations; no street address
core: Web, mobile, API, network and wireless penetration testing, social engineering, source code review, IoT, OT and ICS testing
delivery: Project-based vulnerability assessment and penetration testing
other: ISO 27001 and regulatory consulting, data privacy, managed security, security operations centre
best: Application and network VAPT with compliance consulting
body: Wattlecorp Cybersecurity Labs is a cybersecurity company that provides vulnerability assessment and penetration testing. Its site lists web application, mobile application, API, network and wireless penetration testing, social engineering and secure source code review, plus IoT, OT and ICS testing. The site names the UAE among its locations next to the USA, India and Saudi Arabia, but gives no UAE street address, and it does not list red teaming. Its other services include ISO 27001 and regulatory consulting, a UAE Information Assurance Regulation audit, data privacy services, managed security and a security operations centre. No accreditation is stated in the page text.

name: AHAD
core: Offensive Security unit; penetration testing, red teaming and adversary simulation per a company press release
delivery: Offensive unit inside a multi-service firm
other: Digital forensics, virtual CISO, SOC, managed identity and privileged access
best: An offensive unit within a broader advisory and managed-service firm
body: AHAD is a cybersecurity services company that lists offensive security, digital forensics, virtual CISO, SOC and managed identity services on its site. The offensive security line appears without a service description on the homepage. A company press release describes an Offensive Security Unit covering penetration testing, red teaming, vulnerability management and adversary simulation. The site does not state a headquarters, a founding year or an accreditation, and it shows partner and ISO logos without describing them as certifications. Buyers should request scope, methodology and a sample report directly. AHAD sits in the offensive-led tier because offensive security is listed first among its services, and its public testing detail is the narrowest in that tier.

name: Microminder Cyber Security
core: Infrastructure, web, mobile, cloud, wireless, API, IoT and OT penetration testing; source code review; red and purple teaming
acc: CREST and ISO 27001 (stated by the company)
delivery: Five-step engagement: scoping, signed proposal, delivery, management presentation
other: Managed detection and response, SOC as a service, incident response retainer
best: Buyers consolidating testing and managed security under one vendor
body: Microminder Cyber Security is a managed security provider with a broad offensive testing line. Its site lists infrastructure, web application, mobile, cloud, wireless, API, IoT and ICS or OT penetration testing, source code review, red teaming, purple teaming and breach and attack simulation. The company lists its headquarters on Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai and states CREST and ISO 27001 certifications. It describes a five-step engagement in which delivery starts within 48 hours of sign-off and prerequisites, followed by a management presentation of findings. The same site lists managed detection and response, SOC as a service and an incident response retainer. Microminder describes itself as over four decades in operation.

name: CPX
base: Abu Dhabi (Mohamed Bin Zayed City address listed)
core: Red teaming, vulnerability assessment and penetration testing, purple teaming
acc: Nine ISO certificates stated, not itemised
delivery: Testing within a managed-services and platform portfolio
other: Managed extended detection and response, digital forensics, incident response, threat hunting, threat intelligence
best: Testing alongside managed detection, within a G42 group company
body: CPX is a cybersecurity company, described on its site as a G42 company, that provides red teaming, vulnerability assessment and penetration testing, and purple teaming under security testing and evaluation. It lists an address in Mohamed Bin Zayed City, Abu Dhabi, more than 600 professionals and nine ISO certificates that the page does not itemise. Its other services include managed extended detection and response, digital forensics, incident response, threat hunting and predictive threat intelligence. Offensive work sits inside a managed-services portfolio, so CPX is placed in the managed-security-led tier. The homepage does not describe a testing methodology or a report structure.

name: Obrela
acc: Dubai Cyber Force approval stated in a June 2024 company news item
delivery: Managed detection and response led, with testing as an added service
other: Managed detection and response with a cyber warranty
best: Organisations whose main need is MDR, with testing added
body: Obrela is a managed detection and response provider that also offers penetration testing. Its site describes testing through realistic attack scenarios and advanced adversarial simulations, and it does not use the term red team. Dubai is one of five offices, alongside London, Athens, Riyadh and Cologne. The company states that it serves 250 clients in 25 countries and that its managed detection and response is backed by a cyber warranty. A company news item from June 2024 states Dubai Cyber Force approval for penetration testing and incident response. The homepage names no accreditations in text and gives no founding year. Offensive work is secondary to detection and response, which places Obrela in the managed-security-led tier.

name: Help AG
core: Offensive cybersecurity: red teaming and testing; application security
delivery: Managed security led, with an offensive line
other: Managed security services, cyber SOCs in the UAE and Saudi Arabia
best: Organisations buying managed security that want a red teaming option
body: Help AG is a managed security provider that its site describes as the cybersecurity arm of e& enterprise. Its offensive cybersecurity line is described as red teaming and testing, and application security appears under its zero trust solutions. The company states that it provides services in Dubai and across the Middle East, with cyber SOCs in the UAE and Saudi Arabia. Managed security services are its lead offering, and the site cites an IDC MarketScape 2026 leader designation for Middle East managed security services. The page gives no founding year, names no accreditations and does not describe testing methodology or deliverables. Help AG is placed in the managed-security-led tier.
